comment_regular: Reset a NiD3DShader pass queue before per-geometry setup. Releases every Passes[0..PassCount) slot through NiTArray assignment, releases and nulls CurrentPass, then zeros PassCount and CurrentPassIndex. A subsequent selector-resolution failure therefore cannot reuse a pass from the previous geometry or selector.

DX11 refresh audit: queue reset and pooled pass release prohibit using the prior CurrentPass address as frame-refresh authority. Reconstruct current material producer inputs from owned geometry/property/pass inventory instead.
DX11 replacement audit 2026-10-01: verified x86 queue ownership layout: shader+34 CurrentPassIndex, +38 PassCount, +3C CurrentPass, +40 embedded Passes array. Reset clears every old slot via NiTArray_NiD3DPass_SetAt, then decrements CurrentPass+60 and calls ReleaseToPool on zero before clearing pointer/count/index. These are pass-pool lifecycle effects, distinct from accumulator persistent lists and constant-map NiPointer refs. They remain required when replacing the bucket body. Fallout827C6020 ResetPasses is related by purpose but its body only clears current pass/index; do not infer Oblivion queue release behavior from it.
DX11 queue audit 2026-10-01: preserve release ordering even if next selected pass aliases a prior queue/current object. An intermediate zero ref invokes7604D0 before any new retain; final net deltas cannot suppress that retirement. Initialized, nonretiring paths can coalesce under exclusive all-reference-writer/observer and lifetime ownership; pool cleanup and cold sentinel initialization require explicit lifecycle handling.
